english.title: Aid abet a person to threaten with an offensive weapon on school premises

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Legal Aid Sentencing and punishment of offenders Act 2012

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) aided, abetted, counselled and procured, **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), to have with

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

an offensive weapon, namely **(..SPECIFY THE WEAPON..), to which section 139AA of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 applies on school premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SCHOOL PREMISES..), and unlawfully and intentionally threaten another, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON THREATENED..), with that offensive weapon in such a way that there was an immediate risk of serious physical harm to that person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 139AA(1) and (6) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 and section 8 of the Accessories and Abettors Act 1861.

english.notes:
(i)"Article" is defined in section 139(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988.
(ii) "School premises" are defined in section 139A(6) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988.
(iii) The court may find the defendant not guilty of this offence but guilty of an offence under section 139 or 139A of the Act.
(iv) The Offensive Weapons Act 2019 amended the offence to include an objective element - whether a reasonable person exposed to the threat would think there was an immediate risk of physical harm - and to include further education premises. For offences committed on or after 6th April 2022 see H20307.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 4 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction increased from 2nd May 2022. This applies only to offences committed on or after that date. For offences committed before 2nd May 2022 the maximum penalty on summary conviction is six months.

For minimum sentence for this offence see section 312 of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
